title: The USO show that wrecked camps around the world
summary: With a guitarist, pianist, bass player and drummer she toured World War II theaters; the soldiers wrote ahead to other camps and thousands crowded around.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: But you did -- you did an awful lot of traveling there in the '50's and '40's (inaudible).
You were in Korea during the Korean War. You were in the Pacific during World War II.
And in Europe during World War II --
That's right. And in China, Burma-India

theater, played the whole part of it, all through it, see? Took the first Negro unit called Rhythm and the Blues, and what a group I had! I had a guitar player, a piano player and a drummer, and they -- and a bass man -- and talk about masters.
Oh, we used to wreck those shows.
Who was with you? Do you remember the musicians?

A boy named Ollie from Chicago, and he was on -- what did Ollie play? Ollie played -- let me see, Al played piano. Ollie played drums, and that other boy -- what was his name that -- oh, Al played bass. Ollie played drums. Ollie played --guitar.
You don't remember their last names? (Inaudible).

Yeah, I'm going to get it because they were marvelous. And the boy that played piano, they were marvelous. We used to wreck that show, and I would sing, (If I could be with you one hour tonight, sings) and the fellows would holler -- uh-huh -- and I would holler, suffer, you dog.

And that was -- they used to -- evidently used to write from camp to camp, and they'd tell the different ones to be sure to watch my show, and when we'd get there, we'd wreck that show. I mean wreck the place.
